artifact: CP1 — Lane B planner adversarial checkpoint, pre-build
missionPremise: Three cards, dispatched in one session: G-89 (the lens flash, row A-072) first because it is what a prospect sees; G-88 items 4 and 5 (recount, wrap, re-sync) as one coupled lane because the kit's SHIPPED.size===109 pin passes only while it vendors a stale shell.css; and G-88 items 6/7/9/10 (the design pass), of which item 7 is the only item in the card with NO instrument behind it. The governing finding carried in from 2026-08-19 is that three premises the G-88 work was scoped on were measured false, each caught by an executor measuring rather than reasoning. This checkpoint therefore records the planner's own premise re-checks BEFORE dispatch rather than after.
completionPredicate: G-89 merged and deployed with a probe that was watched failing on the pre-fix build. G-88 items 4 and 5 merged, the class-vocabulary denominator recounted rather than forecast, the four families wrapped as components, and the bundle delta re-synced to Design project f5e5465e-943f-4f68-b52f-608925bc07b0 with sentinel first and _ds_sync.json last and alone. G-88 item 7 merged with a test that fails on a removed id. Items 6/9/10 shipped surface by surface, merged serially, and walked with GET on the deployed service.
scopeBasis: The eleven-item WDLL at _inbox/2026-08-18_g88_design_into_apps_WDLL.md is the contract and items 2, 3 and 8 are already done. Items 1 and 11 are standing. That leaves 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10 plus G-89. Item 6 depends on item 5, so the design pass cannot start until the kit wraps the families; item 7 depends only on item 3, which is done, so it parallelises. That dependency reading is what makes three concurrent executors correct rather than two serial ones.

adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.risk: Two executors in one repo. B89 and B887 both branch from dashboards main.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.assessment: Real but bounded. B89 owns web/index.html, web/shell.css and a new test; B887 is forbidden from touching those three shipping files and owns src/ test space. Separate clones, so no working-tree collision. The residual is merge order.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.mitigation: Merge B89 first per the operator's ordering, then rebase B887 and re-run CI on the rebased head rather than trusting the pre-rebase green. Both PRs are graded on the check-run conclusion string after the rebase, not before.

adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.risk: B887 could pin an exact id count, which B89's merge would then break.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.assessment: The dispatch asks them to reconcile against 94/14/33/10, not to pin it. If they pin, the rebase catches it as a red CI rather than as a silent drift.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.mitigation: Named here so it is checked at merge rather than discovered.

adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.risk: B89 reaches for !important to win the cascade.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.assessment: It would pass a naive review and fail the repo. src/hidden-rule.test.mjs invariant 4 asserts that NO rule other than the single [hidden] rule declares display with !important, precisely so the hidden attribute keeps winning as the stylesheet grows. An !important display rule on .lens would break it.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.mitigation: Left to the hook rather than to the brief, deliberately. This is a mechanized control that already exists and will fire on npm test; DEV_PROCESS rule 0 says a control that depends on the agent remembering is not a control, and one that fires on its own does not need restating. Recorded here so that if it DOES fire, the cause is already understood.

adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.risk: The item 5 coverage assertion goes red on thirty classes and an executor weakens it instead of wrapping them.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.assessment: This is the single most likely way item 5 produces a green PR that is worth nothing. An exclusion set, a 'structural class' carve-out, or a pin lowered to match reality all pass CI.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.mitigation: The dispatch forbids all three by name and says the redness IS the work list.

adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.risk: The four families get wrapped in a shape that reverses what their CSS was built to express.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.assessment: Three specific inversions are available and each would pass every gate: a Cite.model with a children slot re-opens the licensed-text leak the missing slot exists to prevent; an mx API that defaults to pass or makes pass loud reverses inverted applicability; a Meter composable without its basis line re-creates the bare-confidence defect one layer up.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.mitigation: All three named explicitly in the dispatch as traps, with the reason, not as style preferences.

adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.risk: The item 7 instrument is built and is vacuous.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.assessment: Highest-probability failure in the whole session, because the vacuous version is green and looks finished. Four distinct ways: missing ids passed through helper functions like setText(); requiring ids that app.js itself creates, which forces a permanently-red gate and then an allow-list nobody recomputes; scanning only web/index.html when three other sources are served or baked; and putting the clean arm and the injected arm in different tests.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.mitigation: All four named in the dispatch with their incident precedents. The acceptance is red AND NAMED on an injected removal, per category.

adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.risk: The planner's own numbers are wrong and get believed.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.assessment: DEV_PROCESS 3.2. The G-88 scoping pass already produced three different denominators from three investigations and all three were wrong.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.mitigation: Every dispatch states in its own words that reporting a planner figure as wrong is a successful outcome, and each carries the raw evidence for the figures it hands over so an executor can check rather than trust.

adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.risk: The design pass (items 6, 9, 10) is the biggest chunk and is not dispatched yet.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.assessment: Deliberate, not an oversight. Item 6 depends on item 5; designing from kit components that do not yet wrap the four families would produce screens that cannot ship. Dispatching it now would mean an executor inventing the assembly, which is exactly the failure the wrapper exists to prevent.
adversarialReviewOfThisPlan.mitigation: Sequenced after B8845 merges and the bundle re-syncs. Recorded so that a successor can tell a deliberate hold from a dropped item.

plannerOwnedLegsNotDelegated: Merging every PR, in the order named, on the CI check-run conclusion string.

The DesignSync re-sync of the item 5 delta to project f5e5465e-943f-4f68-b52f-608925bc07b0. Not delegated because it is an outward-facing write to a shared external project and because the sequence (sentinel first, chunk by BYTES, reconcile the remote BEFORE arming the anchor, _ds_sync.json last and alone, STOP on any write failure retries do not clear) is the part that cost a session when it was got wrong.
Every Cloud Run deploy and the post-deploy walk.
All verification of executor deliverables. Verification never delegates below the lane planner.
carriedNamedNotBuilt: .prov.stale is absent from every shipped stylesheet and every component in both repos: grep for 'stale' returns nothing in web/shell.css, kit vendor/shell.css, kit src/, web/app.js or web/index.html. So a stale source currently renders identical to a current one. This is a live honesty defect and the WDLL puts it explicitly out of scope and says it wants its own row. Rowing it separately rather than folding it, because shipping it is a three-step cross-repo chain (product CSS, re-vendor, kit component prop) and a drive-by would land the CSS without the component or the component without the CSS.

roster-lens ships on five sections of web/index.html and is defined in neither stylesheet, holding permanent amnesty in two exclusion lists. Folded into the design pass rather than done now, because the roster shells are the first PR in the item 9 merge order and that PR edits those exact five sections. Both concurrent dashboards executors are told not to touch it.
